chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Iss ibn al-Qasim from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who prayed while traveling and completed the prayer. He said, 'If the time [for that prayer] was still present, let him repeat it; and if the time had passed, then no [he does not need to repeat].' And this report does not contradict what has been narrated:

key_terms.أَتَمَّ الصَّلَاةَ: completed the prayer (prayed four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.فِي الْوَقْتِ: within the time (the valid period for the prayer has not yet ended)
key_terms.قَدْ مَضَى: has passed (the time for the prayer has expired)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who mistakenly prays four rak'ahs instead of two?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between *qasr* (shortening) and *tamam* (completing) prayers for travelers, emphasizing that the validity of the completed prayer depends on whether it was performed within its designated time frame. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the conditions under which a traveler must repeat a four-rak'ah prayer, reflecting the principle that prayer validity is tied to both intention and timing. The chain of narration through Safwan ibn Yahya highlights the reliability of this transmission within the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* corpus.
